Laponian area, Sweden

Laponia is a vast wilderness of ancient forests, glaciers, mountains, and sweeping wetlands—spanning approximately 3,600 square miles. A sanctuary for nature enthusiasts, most of this region is preserved within national parks and nature reserves.

The climate here is dramatic: winter plunges to -40°F, while summer can reach highs of 86°F. The Sámi, the area’s Indigenous people, recognize eight distinct seasons, guided by natural cycles and the reindeer migration patterns.

For hiking, late summer to early autumn offers the best conditions—fewer mosquitoes and abundant wild berries. In contrast, winter transforms the landscape into a pristine domain perfect for cross-country skiing across frozen marshes and lakes.
